steps.title: Set up your workbench
actions: Choose filament colors, paint or both.
If you paint, keep paint off nut pockets, threads, mating faces and adhesive contact areas.
Let the paint cure for the time on its label before assembly.
Gather the tools in the {tools}.
Sort the screws by size.
Keep each servo’s horn and center screw together.
Solder and insulate loose parts on the bench, before you mount them.
Where wire length depends on the fit, test-route the wire first. To test-route, run the wire along its final path without fixing or soldering it.
Mark the length. Take the parts back to the bench to solder and heat-shrink them.
steps.check: Your colors are chosen, your tools are ready and your screws are sorted.

steps.title: Slice and print the plates
actions: Open the all-plates Bambu project in Bambu Studio.
Select your printer, nozzle and build plate.
Map each plate’s material profile to one of your spools.
Keep the supplied orientations, supports, support blockers and brims.
Leave “Synchronize filament list from AMS” off.
Slice one plate at a time. Inspect each slice before you print it.
Turn bed leveling on. Turn timelapse off.
Print plates 2 and 7 first. They hold the base and its panels and grilles.
For plate 2, turn flow dynamics calibration off. The printer’s calibration line crosses that plate’s front brim.
Print the other plates as you build. The plate layouts above show the suggested order, the parts and the estimates.
steps.check: Plates 2 and 7 are printed with their supplied settings.

steps.title: Clean and check each print
actions: Let each part cool before you remove its supports.
Remove supports and brims in small pieces.
While you work, support thin fingers, eye housing lips, horn seats, antenna turns, threads and nut-channel ledges.
On the backpack shell (P35), support the belt tabs while you clear the hinge gaps and lower screw passages.
Clear the P35 pin holes.
In the base (FB01), clear the small support lips from the front nut-entry channels.
Clear the screw holes, cable slots and exposed nut pockets in the base. The nut pockets hold the board, bottom cover, grille, power jack plate and audio cradle nuts.
Smooth rough edges at the central wire hole. Do not enlarge the hole.
On the audio cradle (FB24), clear the end windows and lid-nut slots.
Clear support from the horn recesses in both upper arms (AR01, AR04).
Test-fit the real screws, nuts and mating parts. Do not force them. Test-fit means fitting parts without glue or final tightening, and removing them afterwards.
Check how the eyes, eye housings and head shelf (P08) fit the head shell (GS20).
Set aside cracked, warped or delaminated parts for reprinting.
steps.check: The base, its grilles and the rear vent are clean. Their screw holes, nut pockets and cable paths are clear. You know which plate holds the next parts.

safety.text: The plastic behind the front nuts is thin. Too much force can crack it. Clear the channels without thinning that plastic.

steps.title: Fit the board and cover nuts
actions: Place the empty base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Fit and glue one group of nuts at a time. Start with the board nuts.
Push each nut into its pocket without glue. Match its flats to the pocket and its hole to the screw bore. Do not force it.
With a toothpick, put a tiny dab of mixed epoxy (C09) between the nut’s exposed outside edge and the pocket. You can use CA gel (C18) instead. It sets faster.
Keep glue out of threads, screw bores, sliding channels and flat mounting faces.
Keep the glued face up until the glue holds, before you turn the base.
Seat eight M2 nuts in the board pockets: four for the Pi and two for each level shifter.
Seat four M3 nuts in the bottom cover recesses, one at each corner.
Leave the bottom cover off.
steps.check: The eight board nuts and four cover nuts sit flat in their pockets. No glue is in their threads.

panels.title: Glue each nut at its edge

steps.title: Fit the grille and vent nuts
actions: Fit and glue these nuts as in {step:board-cover-nuts}.
From inside the base, slide four M3 nuts upward into the front grille slots.
Turn the base so the rear vent nut slots face up.
From inside, place four M3 nuts in the open slots. Line up each threaded hole with its screw bore.
On each side, slide four M3 nuts upward into the mounting channels. These eight nuts hold the side grilles’ outer holes.
steps.check: The front, rear and side nuts sit flat in their slots. No glue is in their threads.

panels.title: Fit the four front grille nuts

safety.text: The plastic behind the front nuts is thin. Too much force can crack it. Support the plastic behind the nuts while you work.

panels.title: Fit the four rear vent nuts
Fit the eight side grille nuts

steps.title: Fit the cradle and power jack nuts
actions: Fit and glue these nuts as in {step:board-cover-nuts}.
With the base’s open bottom facing up, place three M3 nuts in the open recesses behind the front opening.
Let the glue cure before you mount the audio cradle. The glue holds these nuts while the screws go in.
Turn the base so the power jack nut slots face up.
From inside, fit two M3 nuts. Line up their threaded holes with the screw bores of the power jack plate.
Let the glue cure fully, for the time on its label.
Check gently that every nut in the base stays seated. Start a matching screw in each thread by hand. Do not drive it against the plastic.
Remove the test screws. Leave the base empty.
steps.check: All 33 base nuts (8 M2 and 25 M3) stay seated. Every screw starts freely by hand. The board and cover seating faces are clear.

panels.title: Fit the three audio cradle nuts
Fit the two power jack nuts

steps.title: Fit the front grille and rear vent
actions: Place the empty base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Find the front opening. The front microphone grille (FB41) fits here.
Find the rear opening. The rear vent (FB03) fits here.
At the front opening, hold the grille against the outside of the base. Put four M3×6 screws through the grille into the fitted nuts. Use no washers.
Start all four screws by hand. Tighten them evenly.
If a screw does not start by hand, remove it. Check that its nut is seated.
At the rear opening, hold the rear vent against the outside of the base. Put four M3×12 screws through the vent into the fitted nuts. Use no washers.
Start all four screws by hand. Tighten them evenly.
Leave the bottom of the base open.
steps.check: Both parts sit flat. Each nut stays seated and the plastic around it is not cracked.

steps.title: Attach the speakers to their grilles
actions: Place one speaker (E16) against the inside of a loose side speaker grille (FB19). Face its cone toward the grille opening.
Line up the four speaker tabs with the four inner holes of the grille.
From the outside, insert four M3×12 screws through the grille and speaker tabs. On the speaker side, add one M3 washer and one M3 nut to each screw.
Hold each nut while you tighten its screw until snug. Keep the speaker tabs flat.
Repeat for the second speaker. Leave both speaker cables unplugged.
steps.check: Both speakers are held firmly against their grilles. Screw tips clear the speaker housing and cables.
steps.note: You mount these grilles on the base in {step:side-grilles}.

panels.title: Face the cone toward the grille
Screw the speaker to the grille

steps.title: Mount the side speaker grilles
actions: Pass one speaker cable through a side opening of the base. Keep the cable clear of the mounting edge.
Hold the side speaker grille (FB19) flat against the outside of the base.
Put four M3×12 screws through its outer holes into the fitted nuts. Use no washers. Repeat on the other side.
Label each speaker cable with its side: robot-left or robot-right.
Leave enough cable slack to pull a grille away for service.
Leave the plugs disconnected until {step:audio-module}.
steps.check: Both grilles sit flat. The speakers and cables are inside the base, with no cable pinched under an edge.

steps.title: Fit the feet
actions: Choose four matching adhesive feet (E25) that fit on the base’s Ø14 mm post faces.
Clean and dry the four post faces.
Peel the backing from one foot. Center it on a post face. Press it on firmly.
Let the adhesive bond for the time on its label before you load the feet.
Stand the base upright. Check that it does not rock. The bottom cover must clear the feet.
steps.check: The base stands level on four firmly bonded feet.

steps.title: Set up your computer and SSH key
actions: Install Git, Make, Python 3.12 or newer, OpenSSH (ssh and scp), and Raspberry Pi Imager on your computer. Check the terminal commands below before continuing; python3 must select your supported Python.
On Windows, use WSL for every terminal command in this guide, including key creation, cloning and Make. Run Imager in Windows; import the public key from that same WSL environment.

Use an existing SSH key from the terminal environment you will use to connect. If you have no key, run ssh-keygen below and follow its prompts. Never overwrite an existing key: answer no if it asks to replace one.

For the default key name, display id_ed25519.pub with the second command. Keep the entire public-key line for Imager. The file without .pub is private; never paste or share it. If your key has another name, use that .pub path and select its private key through your SSH agent or an IdentityFile rule for this Pi.

steps.title: Choose the Pi, system and card
actions: Open Imager and choose Raspberry Pi 3 for the Pi 3 Model A+ (E09).
Choose Raspberry Pi OS (other), then Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit). Confirm that the description names Trixie. The installer requires 64-bit Trixie with Python 3.13.

Insert the microSD card (E13) in your computer’s card reader. Select that card in Imager and check its name and capacity. Writing erases the selected drive; stop if you cannot identify it confidently.

steps.title: Set the Pi name, account and Wi-Fi
actions: Choose a unique hostname, for example `blooglyblob`. Write down your hostname and the username you choose next; you will use both for SSH and the repository settings.
In Localisation, choose your country/capital city, time zone and keyboard layout, then continue to User.
Choose a username and password for the Pi. This guide uses builder as its example username. Keep the password private and available for sudo prompts; do not put it in the repository settings.
Enter your Wi-Fi network name and password. The Pi and your computer must be able to reach each other on the network; the Pi also needs internet access.

steps.title: Enable SSH and write the card
actions: Enable SSH and select public-key authentication. Paste your public-key line or select the .pub file you prepared. Do not use Imager’s automatically suggested key unless it is the key from your command environment.

On Windows, a Windows SSH key and a WSL SSH key are different files. Paste the output of cat from WSL, or select its .pub file through the WSL filesystem; do not switch terminal environments for later commands.
Leave Raspberry Pi Connect off; this build uses SSH. Review the Pi, OS, storage and custom settings, then start writing. Wait for writing and verification to finish, eject the card, and continue.

steps.title: Boot and connect to the Pi
actions: With power disconnected, insert the prepared microSD card into the Pi. Rest the bare board on a clean, nonconductive surface.
Connect the separate 5 V, 2.5 A micro-USB bench supply (T13) to the Pi’s micro-USB power port. Allow a few minutes for the first boot and Wi-Fi connection.
In your computer terminal, replace builder and blooglyblob in the example with the username and hostname you recorded. Connect using the same environment and SSH key you used for Imager.

If .local does not resolve, find the Pi’s IP address in your router’s device list and use it instead. On the first connection, confirm you are contacting that Pi before accepting its host key. Stop at a changed-host-key warning; verify a reimage or changed destination before correcting known_hosts.

A shell prompt containing the Pi’s username and hostname means you are connected. If access is denied, check the Imager username and that its public key matches your SSH key; do not continue with a different account by guessing.
Type exit to leave the Pi shell. Leave the Pi powered for configuration in the next step.
steps.check: You connected to the Pi with your SSH key, then returned to your computer’s terminal.

steps.title: Get the code and add your settings
actions: On your computer, clone the repository and enter its folder. If you already have this checkout, enter that folder instead; do not create another copy inside it. Run later Make commands from this repository folder.
The commands below copy each example only if its destination does not exist. Keep existing settings; never replace them with a fresh example during a rerun.
Open .env in a text editor. Set PI_HOST to your recorded hostname plus .local, or the IP address that worked for SSH; set PI_USER to your chosen username. Keep BLOOGLYBLOB_ENV_FILE=config/app.env.
The example below matches blooglyblob and builder. These are file settings, not terminal commands. Do not add your Pi password or Wi-Fi password.
Create an API key for your own OpenAI account and enable API billing. API usage is separate from a ChatGPT subscription; your account needs access to the models listed in config/app.env.example.

Open config/app.env in your editor and put the key after OPENAI_API_KEY=. Keep the other example settings. This ignored file is private: do not commit it, share it or show it in screenshots. Application startup can make a billable greeting request; conversations also use paid API services.

steps.title: Find and set the audio device
actions: Plug the USB extension’s male end (E23) into the Pi’s USB-A socket, then connect the audio module (E14) to its female socket. Keep the module in its case on the bench.
From the repository folder on your computer, open SSH using .env. If the target is wrong or unreachable, fix PI_HOST and PI_USER before continuing.
On the Pi, list the sound cards. Note the USB name after USB-Audio - and its bracketed card ID (Device in this example). Use the ID for mixer commands; the numeric index can change after reboot.
If no USB audio card appears, check the module and extension connections, then run the command again.

For this USB module, read the Speaker control, set playback to −40 dB and save it. Replace Device with your card ID. Both channels should report [-40.00dB]. If the control or dB scale is missing, inspect it with alsamixer -c Device before proceeding.
This is a low starting level; adjust gradually during the later speaker check. Recheck with amixer -c Device sget Speaker after reboot. Type exit to return to your computer.
Back on your computer, edit config/app.env. Set AUDIO_INPUT_DEVICE and AUDIO_OUTPUT_DEVICE to the actual USB audio name you noted. Remove the leading # if editing the commented examples.

The selected module provides both microphone and speaker audio, so both settings use that same device name. A missing or ambiguous name stops application startup instead of silently choosing another device.
Set MIC_GAIN=1 initially so the microphone has no added software amplification. This does not control speaker volume. Tune it only after a voice test.
steps.check: Your computer has the correct Pi target, private API settings and USB audio names. The USB playback level is saved at −40 dB; microphone software gain starts at 1.

steps.title: Install the software
actions: On your computer, run the prerequisite check from the repository folder. It must identify your intended Pi 3, aarch64 or arm64, Python 3.13 and Trixie.
If it rejects the model or OS, stop and correct the board/image selection in {step:imager-choose}. If SSH fails, fix the connection in {step:pi-connect}; do not proceed past a failed check.

Keep servo and lighting circuits disconnected, then run provisioning. It installs dependencies and starts the application, which also starts on boot. Enter the Pi account password if sudo requests it; it is not saved in .env.

If provisioning succeeds, continue to the status check. If it asks for a reboot because snd_bcm2835 is loaded, follow the next panel, then rerun provisioning. For any other failure, fix the reported cause before continuing.
If provisioning reports the built-in audio module, open the Pi shell and reboot it. SSH disconnecting during reboot is expected. This frees the timer the lighting driver needs.
Wait for the Pi to rejoin Wi-Fi, then rerun make pi-provision from your computer. Provisioning preserves existing remote settings; there is no extra pi-update step for first installation.

steps.title: Check the service and shut down
actions: Check the service status. It should show active (running). If it is stopped or failed, inspect its logs next instead of marking setup complete.

Follow the application log. If it reports a missing key or audio device, correct the installed settings on the Pi as described below; changing the initial file on your computer does not replace an existing remote file.
Press Ctrl+C to stop following logs and return to your computer prompt. Do not run microphone, lighting or servo tests here; those checks follow hardware assembly.
If the log identifies a configuration error, open SSH and edit /etc/blooglyblob/app.env with sudoedit. Correct the key or device name, save and close the editor, then type exit.
Back on your computer, restart and recheck the service. Skip this panel if the service is already running without configuration errors.
From your computer, open the Pi shell and shut it down. The SSH session will disconnect.
Wait for the Pi’s green activity light to stop flashing, then unplug the bench supply and USB audio lead. Continue to {step:pi-shifters} with the board unpowered.

steps.title: Mount the Pi and level shifters
actions: Label the two level shifters (E15) as level shifter (S1) and level shifter (S2).
On the back of each board, find the copper jumper labeled Neo, beside the top mounting hole. Cutting it disables only the onboard test LED.
Cut only the narrow bridge inside its white outline. With the meter in continuity mode, check that each cut is open. Both signal channels on each board stay active.
Place the base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Find the Pi mounts at the rear and the two level shifter positions in front of them.
Mark S1 nearer the Pi and S2 nearer the audio cradle.
Mark GPIO pin 1 beside the Pi header. Pin 1 is at the microSD end, farthest from the full-size USB port. Its underside pad is square.
Place the Pi (E09) with its components toward the open bottom. Point its full-size USB port toward the audio cradle and its microSD end toward the rear wall.
Check that the USB and power plugs fit without pressing on nearby parts. Fit four M2×12 screws. Tighten them only until secure, without bowing the board.
Fit S1 in the position nearer the Pi and S2 in the position nearer the audio cradle. Face their components and screw heads toward the open bottom.
Fasten each board with two M2×10 screws into the seated nuts. Use no washers.
Keep the terminal entries and both frame-screw paths clear.
steps.check: All three boards sit flat and their nuts stay bonded. Screw tips clear components. The sockets stay reachable.
steps.note: You fitted the eight board nuts in {step:board-cover-nuts}.

steps.title: Mount and label the four WAGOs
actions: Clean and dry the backs of the four WAGOs (E06) and their pads in the base. Follow the mounting tape (C16) instructions.
Cut a piece of tape to fit the flat back of each WAGO. Keep it clear of the levers and wire entries.
Place each WAGO with its wire entries toward the robot’s front and its levers toward the open bottom.
Test-fit all four WAGOs with the tape thickness included. Each lever must open fully without touching the cover or nearby parts.
Remove the liners. Press each WAGO onto its pad. Let the tape bond for its stated time before wiring.
Beside the pads, label the four WAGOs from rear to front.
Rear to front: input WAGO (W1), ground WAGO (W3), servo power WAGO (W2), servo ground WAGO (W4). W1 and W2 carry +5 V. W3 and W4 carry GND.
Open and close each lever gently to check the bond.
Number each WAGO’s ports from the robot-right end. In this open-bottom view, port 1 is on the picture’s right.
All five ports in one WAGO are joined.
Use this numbering for all four WAGOs. In this guide, W1/3 means WAGO W1, port 3.

steps.title: Mount the audio cradle
actions: On the loose audio cradle (FB24), slide an M2 nut sideways into each end pocket. Work from the middle outward.
Keep the nut flats parallel to the slot walls.
With the open bottom of the base facing up, place the cradle inside it, directly behind the front microphone grille. Keep it clear of the grille screw tips.
Put three M3×6 screws through the cradle into the fitted nuts. Use no washers. Fit the middle screw now. The audio module will cover it.
Start all three screws by hand. Tighten them gently.
steps.check: The empty cradle is screwed to the base at all three mounting holes. Both M2 lid nuts are seated.
steps.note: You fitted the cradle nuts in {step:cradle-jack-nuts}. The lid screws go into the lid nuts in {step:audio-module}.

steps.title: Fit the USB audio module
actions: Check that the USB extension socket passes through the cradle end opening without force. If it does not, leave the module out. The cable route or connector fit needs resolving first.
Clean the back of the USB audio module (E14) case and the inside rear wall of the cradle. Follow the tape instructions.
Apply double-sided tape (C16) under 1 mm thick to the back of the case, opposite the microphones. Keep it inside the flat face. Do not tape the lid.
Remove the outer tape liner.
With both cables disconnected, lift the module into the cradle. Face its microphones toward the front grille.
Keep the tape clear of the wall until the case is seated.
Press the case rearward so the tape bonds to the inside rear wall. Use the pressure and bonding time in the tape instructions.
Through the end openings, connect the USB data extension (E23), 200 mm or shorter.
Connect the four-wire speaker cable. Connect each labeled speaker to its matching output. The speaker outputs do not connect to power ground.
Leave the Pi end of the USB extension disconnected until {step:button-audio-wiring}.
Line the audio cradle lid (FB32) with 1 mm foam (C10). Keep its openings clear.
Fit the lid with two M2×8 screws into the cradle nuts. Use no washers. Tighten gently, without squeezing the case or trapping cables.
Check that the tape holds the case and that the microphones and plugs stay clear.

steps.title: Prepare the button leads
actions: On the back of the button (E17), find the LED and switch terminals. Label each one.
The closer upper pair is LED − and LED +. The wider lower pair is the switch.
With the meter in continuity mode, check that the lower switch pair closes only while you press the button.
On the bench, slide heat-shrink onto four GPIO jumper leads (E24).
Solder the four quick-connect wires (E19) to the four GPIO leads. Keep the female sockets at the Pi ends.
Add the button LED resistor (R1), 1 kΩ, in the LED-positive lead.
Insulate every splice and both resistor joints.
Label each Pi end with its Pi pin. Switch leads: pins 11 and 14. LED + lead through R1: pin 4. LED − lead: pin 20.
Leave the four Pi ends disconnected until {step:button-audio-wiring}.
steps.check: Every joint on the button leads is insulated. Each Pi end is labeled with its pin.

steps.title: Fit the front button
actions: Beneath the button opening, load two M3 nuts into the base.
Push the inner nut upward into its pocket.
Beside the foot post, slide the other nut sideways in from the button opening. Line up its flats with the pocket.
On the bench, put the button (E17) through the button insert (FB20) from the outside.
Tighten the button’s supplied retaining nut against the back of the insert.
Push the prepared quick-connects onto their matching terminals. Cover exposed contact metal with separate insulating sleeves.
Keep the connectors removable. Keep the insulated joints clear of the retaining nut.
Route the leads into the base. Leave enough slack to remove the insert.
Hold the insert flush in its opening, clear of the screw bosses and foot post.
Fit two M3×8 screws from the outside. Use no washers. Tighten gently. Do not use the screws to pull the insert into place.
steps.check: All soldered joints are insulated and the switch closes only when pressed. The button insert sits flush without pinching its leads. The four labeled Pi ends stay disconnected.

steps.title: Prepare and fit the power jack
actions: On the bench, away from printed parts, find the center-pin and sleeve lugs of the power jack (J1). Use the meter in continuity mode.
The center pin is +5 V. The sleeve is the return. The third, switched lug stays unused.
Solder an 18 AWG lead to each of those two lugs. Label each lead with its function. The return lead may need 150–160 mm.
Insulate each joint and the unused switched lug separately.
With the meter in continuity mode, check each lead again. Check that there is no short between center and sleeve.
Let the joints cool before mounting. Leave the leads long for final routing.
Feed the prepared leads through the power jack plate (FB21). Fit J1 into the plate with its supplied washer and nut on the outside.
Check full thread engagement and clearance around the insulated lugs.
Seat the plate flush. Fasten it from outside with two M3×12 screws. Use no washers.
Leave enough lead slack to remove the plate.
steps.check: The jack cannot rotate. The center and sleeve leads are labeled and insulated. The plate comes off without pulling a joint.

steps.title: Connect the power jack, Pi power lead and ground
actions: Leave both fuses out. Route and trim the inlet leads to their labeled ports.
Strip 11 mm for each WAGO 221-415 port. Insert one bare, untinned wire fully, close the lever and gently pull-check it.
Keep the micro-B plug on the Adafruit 4056 lead. Identify +5 V at plug pin 1 and return at pin 5 by continuity; insulate other conductors individually.

Dry-route, trim and strip the two supply wires, then land them and plug H2 into the Pi power socket. The finished 24 AWG lead, including the plug, must be 150 mm or shorter, without an extension or service loop.
Fit the ground link with 11 mm stripped at each end. Leave W1/5 and W4/5 empty.
steps.check: Inlet center reaches W1, sleeve reaches W3/W4, H2 polarity is correct and its total length is no more than 150 mm.
