panels.title: Seat each wire in its WAGO port
Identify the H2 supply wires
panels.caption: Pi power: H2 +5 V → W1/2; H2 return → W3/2.

panels.title: Route the short Pi power lead
panels.caption: Use gentle bends through the gaps in the WAGO row. Check the actual lead reaches before trimming.

panels.title: Join the two ground connectors
panels.caption: One 18 AWG wire: W3/3 → W4/1.

steps.title: Wire the servo fuse and capacitor
actions: Label one holder F1. Dry-route its loop from W1/3 to W2/1, then mark and cut where both ends reach without tension.
If the output needs length, solder an 18 AWG extension on the bench and insulate the joint. Do not extend the input; change the layout instead.
Strip 11 mm and land both leads, leaving the holder accessible for opening. Keep W2/2–4 for the three servos.
Solder 18 AWG leads to C1 on the bench, preserving polarity. Cover each leg and joint separately with heat-shrink.
Land one wire in each assigned WAGO port. Leave gentle bends at the capacitor’s rubber-seal end and keep its vent end uncovered.
steps.check: F1 is the only path from W1 to W2, C1 polarity is correct and its two insulated leads are separate.

panels.title: Prepare F1
panels.caption: F1 uses a T3.15 A fuse; keep the cartridge out for wiring.

panels.title: Land F1
panels.caption: W1/3 → F1 → W2/1. No direct W1-to-W2 link.

panels.title: Prepare and land C1
panels.caption: 1000 µF, 10 V: positive → W2/5; striped negative → W3/4.

steps.title: Wire the light fuse and capacitor
actions: Label the second holder F2. Dry-route its loop from W1/4 to the base half of BASE→BODY, called H3. Mark and cut only when both ends reach.
Use 18 AWG for any output extension, soldered and insulated on the bench. Do not extend the input.
Choose one E10 three-pin JST-SM pair for BASE→BODY. Label each contact +5 V, GND or DATA and confirm that the two halves match by continuity.
Join C2 positive to the H3 +5 V branch from F2 output. Join C2 striped negative to H3 return. Keep the connector’s 22 AWG power wires and branches separate.
Make and insulate both branch joints on the bench. No bare lead or solder should touch another conductor or the printed parts.
Strip the WAGO ends to 11 mm and land one wire per port. Leave H3 DATA labeled for the next step and BASE→BODY unplugged.
steps.check: F2 feeds H3 positive, C2 polarity is correct and all branch joints are individually insulated.

panels.title: Prepare F2
panels.caption: F2 uses a T1 A fuse; keep the cartridge out for wiring.

panels.title: Prepare H3 and C2
panels.caption: C2 is 1000 µF, 10 V. It stays on the base side of the connector.

panels.title: Insulate the branch joints
panels.caption: Slide heat-shrink on before soldering; cover each polarity separately.

panels.title: Land the lighting feed
panels.caption: F2 input → W1/4; H3 return including C2 negative → W3/5.

steps.title: Connect the level shifters
actions: Prepare the remaining eight GPIO leads for the shifter inputs, keeping the 2.54 mm female socket at each Pi end. Remove any connector at the other end and strip only enough insulation for the bare wire to fit fully inside its screw terminal.
Hold the plastic socket and push it straight down onto the physical Pi pin shown in the following wiring diagrams. Each socket fits one pin.
Connect Pi pin 1 to S1 V, pin 6 to G, pin 12 to DAT and pin 32 to CLK. Land H3 DATA on S1 D5; label C5 LEFT.
Insert bare wire fully inside each shifter terminal and tighten, with no exposed strands. Leave !D5 unused.
Connect Pi pin 17 to S2 V, pin 9 to G, pin 33 to DAT and pin 36 to CLK. Leave !D5 unused.

panels.title: Prepare the socket and terminal leads
panels.caption: Prepare eight socket-to-bare-wire leads for the shifters. The four button leads were prepared before the button was mounted.

panels.title: Plug the sockets onto the Pi
Wire S1
panels.caption: Pin-side view, pin 1 at the microSD end. Follow the board’s input labels G, V, DAT and CLK.

panels.title: Wire S2
panels.caption: Same board orientation as S1. S2 D5 is RIGHT; C5 is HEAD. Its Neo trace was cut during board preparation.

steps.title: Connect the button and USB audio
actions: Connect the two prepared switch leads to Pi pin 11 (GPIO17 input) and pin 14 (GND). These lower terminals close only while the button is pressed.

Connect the prepared LED-positive lead, with R1 insulated in line, to Pi pin 4 (+5 V); connect LED − to pin 20 (GND). The Pi header supplies the button light’s power and return. Keep this upper LED pair separate from the lower switch pair.
Connect the audio extension to the Pi’s full-size USB socket and check both speaker plugs. Keep servo outputs labeled but disconnected.
Route the USB cable around the audio cradle with a relaxed bend below it. Keep the cable clear of the bottom cover and avoid pulling sideways on either socket.
steps.check: All twelve Pi header connections match their physical pin numbers, H3 DATA reaches S1 D5, and switch, light and speaker circuits are separate.
steps.note: The button starts a conversation; it does not turn power off.

panels.title: Connect the button switch
panels.caption: Lower switch tabs connect to Pi pins 11 and 14; the LED tabs stay separate.

panels.title: Connect the button light
panels.caption: Pin 4 supplies +5 V; pin 20 is ground. Both button contacts and all soldered joins are insulated.

panels.title: Connect audio to the Pi
panels.caption: USB carries data and power; speaker outputs do not join W3 or W4.

panels.title: Dress the USB cable
panels.caption: Oblique view with the enclosure omitted. Adjust the bend to your cable; the cover must close without pressing on it.

steps.title: Secure the fuses, capacitors and wire bundles
actions: Lay F1 toward the front and F2 toward the rear, with C1 and C2 beside the WAGO row as shown. Keep fuse openings reachable and capacitor vent ends uncovered.
With their liners still on, position 1 × 1-inch adhesive tie squares on flat interior faces. Check full contact and at least 4 mm clearance from wiring and tie locks to the cover.
Apply the squares using their own backing and the maker’s surface preparation and bonding instructions. Check the bonds before loading them.

Tie the bodies and bundles just tightly enough to prevent sliding, clear of capacitor ends and fuse openings. Leave tie locks reachable for cutting and keep plugs, vents, SD card and frame screws accessible. Keep that F2 output section reachable by releasing its nearest tie.

Keep the central opening free for the three servo cables and the three-wire lighting cable. Route stationary bundles around the marked frame-screw paths, with the SD card, WAGO levers and fuse caps accessible.
steps.check: Bodies and bundles are supported independently of terminals, adhesive bonds hold and the cover clears every wire and tie.

panels.title: Dry-layout the bodies and supports
panels.caption: The drawn bodies show placement areas. Put adhesive mounts where your actual wiring needs support.

panels.title: Bond, then tie
panels.caption: Representative mounting detail; choose the position from your actual routing. Keep capacitor ends and fuse openings clear.

panels.title: Keep service access clear
panels.caption: Dashed rings locate the harness opening and frame-screw access. They do not specify a minimum clearance or cable-tie position.

steps.title: Check the unpowered base
actions: Check jack center → W1, sleeve → W3, H2 plug polarity and W3 → W4. There must be no direct W1-to-W2 connection and no sustained +5 V-to-ground short.
Check capacitor polarity and insulated joints. Test each fuse separately; fit F1 T3.15 A to confirm W1 reaches W2 through it, then remove F1 again. Fit F2 T1 A for the next lighting test.
Compare S1, S2 and button wiring to their diagrams. Check each closed WAGO lever and terminal; neither speaker negative connects to ground.
Remove wire offcuts and debris. Check board nuts, screw tips, plug access and cover clearance; keep servos and HEAD disconnected.
steps.check: The unpowered checks pass, F1 is removed, F2 T1 A is fitted and all servo and HEAD connections are still disconnected.

panels.title: Check the supply paths
panels.caption: Remove the fuse cartridges while checking for a bypass.

panels.title: Check header and terminals
panels.caption: Match physical pin numbers, starting at the pin 1 mark.

steps.title: Prepare the body light input
actions: Use Adafruit’s wire markings: copper coil/dots identify +5 V, the middle wire is normally DATA, and the remaining wire is GND. Label them; ask the vendor if markings are missing or disagree.
For the likely input, hold the connector upward with the resin bump facing you and marked +5 V wire on the left. Confirm direction with the light test below.
Prepare the BODY pigtail and separate 22 AWG HEAD power tails. Leave them long until dry-routing in {step:body-light-strand}; keep all 100 pebbles together.
Label the factory leads, then remove only the likely input’s connector, retaining wire length. Solder R2 (330 Ω) between BODY DATA and strand DATA near the first pebble, then insulate both joints.
Branch BODY +5 V to strand +5 V and the HEAD positive tail. Repeat for GND. Insulate both joints and cap the two free HEAD tails separately.

panels.title: Identify the wires and likely input
Add the HEAD power tails now

steps.title: Test the body light input
actions: Check contact mapping and for a +5 V-to-GND short, then plug H3 into BODY. F1 stays out, F2 T1 A stays fitted, servos stay disconnected and HEAD tails stay capped.
Power the supply by itself. With your meter on DC volts, red probe in the plug center and black on its sleeve, check 5.0–5.25 V with no minus sign. Unplug it again.
Connect the supply to the base, then the wall, and let the Pi boot. Stop and unplug if you notice smoke, an unusual smell or overheating.

Run make pi-stop, then make pi-test-neopixels from your computer. It addresses the first 16 pixels at brightness 128 and clears those 16 when finished; software eye/mouth labels still refer to indices on this all-pebble test strand.
If the first 16 pebbles light from the connected end in sequence, mark that end INPUT. The other 84 should remain dark; unplug and investigate unexpected light.

If nothing lights, check power, DATA and contacts first. If those are correct but the strand stays dark, shut down and unplug, move the BODY/R2 harness and its power branches to the other end, and repeat. Insulate the abandoned end’s three wires separately. Mark INPUT only after a positive light test.

Run make pi-ssh, then sudo poweroff; wait for the green light to stop, then unplug. Disconnect BASE→BODY. Keep the prepared input wiring attached and the HEAD tails capped for {step:body-light-strand}. Do not cut between pebbles until an end passes.
steps.check: The connected end passes the light test and is marked INPUT. Its permanent BODY/R2 wiring stays attached; HEAD tails are capped and power is disconnected.

panels.title: Check the supply before connecting
panels.caption: Use the specified Mean Well GST40A05-P1J, 5 V, 5 A.

panels.title: Power the base and run the light test
panels.caption: Connect the barrel plug before powering the supply.

steps.title: Attach the frame uprights
actions: Support the enclosure in the service stand. Place the lower P01 collar and both P02 uprights on its deck.
Load one M3 nut into each upright’s lower side pocket. Insert the screws upward through the enclosure and collar, then tighten evenly.
Check the collar sits flat and both uprights are parallel. Keep the central cable opening clear.
steps.check: Both uprights are firm and parallel, the collar sits flat and no wire is trapped.
steps.note: Keep the head and arms off the servo shafts until {step:shelf-arms}.

panels.title: Place the collar and uprights
panels.caption: The uprights stand at front and back, not the sides.

panels.title: Fasten upward from the base
panels.caption: Two M3×16 screws from below into two side-loaded M3 nuts.

steps.title: Prepare the three servo cables
actions: Identify supply, ground and signal using the Kitronik 25105 datasheet and label each cable at both ends.
Cut off the crocodile clips one wire at a time, preserving the labels. Keep the ends separate.

Hold each loose servo near its mounting position and dry-route to the assigned WAGO and shifter terminals. Mark the needed length, then solder and heat-shrink any extensions on the bench, with joints clear of moving areas.
Prepare supply and return ends for 11 mm WAGO insertion. The signal’s bare end must fit entirely inside its shifter terminal.
steps.check: All three servo cables are labeled, reach their terminals with slack and have insulated extension joints.

panels.title: Label each servo
panels.caption: Prepare LEFT, RIGHT and HEAD cables before fitting the servos.

panels.title: Make any needed extensions
panels.caption: Use 22 AWG extensions if a lead is thinner than 24 AWG or too short.

steps.title: Mount the shoulder servos
actions: On the bench, press four M2 nuts into P03’s inward-facing hex pockets.
Slide each servo sideways from the robot’s back until its ears sit on the supports, with its cable toward the body.
Fit all four ear screws before mounting P03 to the frame. Keep horns off and check each servo sits firm without bowing its ears.
Hold a loose M3 nut in each bracket access well and start both front screws. The wells do not retain these nuts by themselves.
Hold the rear nuts and fit both screws. Tighten all four evenly, keeping the uprights straight. A small gap around a servo body is normal.
steps.check: Neither servo rocks, all ears sit flat and P03 is secure without bowed uprights.

panels.title: Insert both servos from the back
panels.caption: The long side of P03 is open; the shafts point outward.

panels.title: Fasten the ears first
panels.caption: Two M2×6 screws and nuts per servo.

panels.title: Fasten the front of P03
panels.caption: Section view: hold each loose nut while starting its screw.

panels.title: Fasten the rear of P03
panels.caption: Section view: hold each loose nut while starting its screw.

steps.title: Mount the head servo and upper foam collar
actions: Off the frame, press two M2 nuts into P04’s underside hex pockets.
Slide the servo through its open side, ears on the supports and cable toward the body.
Fit both ear screws before mounting the bracket. Check the servo cannot rock or slide.
Fit both screws through P04 and the uprights, holding the far-side nuts. Route the cable down the frame, clear of the head horn.
Load each upright’s upper nut pocket and fasten the second P01 collar from above. Keep the head-bracket screws reachable.
steps.check: P04 is firm, the upper collar is level and the head shaft points upward with a clear cable path.

panels.title: Insert the head servo
panels.caption: The servo enters P04 sideways from robot-left.

panels.title: Fasten its ears
panels.caption: Two M2×6 screws enter downward from above.

panels.title: Mount P04
panels.caption: Two M3×20 screws enter from robot-left; loose M3 nuts sit on the far side.

panels.title: Fit the upper collar
panels.caption: Two M3×10 screws downward into side-loaded M3 nuts. Uprights are cut away to show the nuts.

steps.title: Prepare the three servo horns
actions: Keep each round horn with its center screw. With the horn off its servo, select the opposite pair about 18 mm apart and drill those two holes to 2.2 mm.
Remove burrs and drilling debris. Leave the central spline and center hole unchanged; keep the horns off the shafts until {step:shelf-arms}.
The horn’s long splined hub faces the servo shaft; the flat disk seats against the printed part. Keep each center screw for the fit-pose step.
steps.check: Two M2 screws pass freely through each drilled pair and all three center splines are undamaged.
steps.note: The drawing identifies the hole pair; it is not a drilling template.

panels.title: Drill one opposite pair
panels.caption: Measure the pair on your supplied horn.

panels.title: Recognize the two faces
panels.caption: The profile explains orientation; it is not a dimensioned horn model.

steps.title: Build the head shelf on the bench
actions: Attach one drilled horn to P14. Keep its supplied center screw aside; the assembly stays off the head servo.
Place P14 over P08, fit three M3 nuts above the adapter, and insert the screws from below. Keep the open cable entry clear.
steps.check: The horn, P14 and P08 are secure on the bench; the cable entry and horn center hole remain clear.

panels.title: Fasten the horn to P14
panels.caption: Two M2×6 screws and two M2 nuts use the drilled offset holes.

panels.title: Fasten P14 above the shelf
panels.caption: P14’s flange sits above P08. Three M3×8 screws enter upward from the shelf underside.

steps.title: Fit the eye windows and diffusers
actions: Use the eye template to cut two flexible transparency windows, 12.6 × 8.6 mm with 4.2 mm corner radii. The template has small fit alternatives.
With each housing off the head, gently bow the film into the groove behind its front lip and let it flatten with its whole edge captured. Do not force thick film behind the 0.6 mm lip.
Place a 14 × 10 mm patch of 4 mm white Plastazote LD45 behind each window. Support the housing so the foam stays in place.
steps.check: Both windows sit flat with their edges captured and the foam is not crushed.
steps.note: Any clear flexible transparency sheet is suitable if it fits the groove without forcing the lip.

steps.title: Seat the eye housings
actions: With each housing off the head, slide one standard M2 nut into each channel, flats parallel to the front, until it sits beneath its screw-hole roof. Do not glue them or push them through the round holes.
With film and foam in place, seat GS11 and GS12 in the head. Their short tapered pegs align them; they do not snap in.
Keep the head face-down so the loose nuts and foam stay in place until the cassettes are fastened.
steps.check: Both housings sit without force, each has two seated nuts and the film and foam remain flat.
steps.note: Standard M2 nuts are 4 mm across flats and 1.6 mm thick.

panels.title: Load two nuts in each housing
panels.caption: M2 nuts slide from the upper edge beneath the thin retaining roofs.

panels.title: Seat the housings from the face side
panels.caption: GS11 is robot-right; GS12 is robot-left. The blue cutaway shows the head wall between housing and cassette; fastening comes next.

steps.title: Fit the eye boards and straps
actions: Seat two M2 nuts in each cassette’s rectangular pockets above and below the light opening.
Turn the cassette over, seat the Adafruit 5975 board on its supports and fit two M2×6 screws, no washers. Tighten lightly.
From inside the head, pass each outer screw through its washer, cassette ear and head into the housing nut. Stop when the nuts seat under their roofs; do not force a bottomed-out screw.
Check that both housings sit flat, the screws hold without bottoming out and the retaining roofs remain intact. Keep all four eye sockets accessible.
Dry-fit all three straps and check they clear the eye housing joints. Glue only their locating pegs with the two-part epoxy; let it fully cure.
Check that no glue bridges the housing joints or seams. Do not clamp the rear seams shut.
steps.check: Each eye removes and refits independently, and only the strap locating pegs are glued.
steps.note: Finish both eyes before fitting the mouth, which blocks straight access to the outer eye screws.

panels.title: Load the cassette nuts
panels.caption: Two M2 nuts go on the foam-facing side of each P06.

panels.title: Attach each LED board
panels.caption: LED toward the foam; IN and OUT sockets toward the inside of the head.

panels.title: Fasten each cassette into the head
panels.caption: Two outer M2×10 screws with thin M2 washers per eye.

panels.title: Check both fitted eyes
panels.caption: Fit the eyes before the mouth. Short screws hold the boards; outer screws hold the cassettes.

panels.title: Glue only the strap pegs
panels.caption: Inner faces: glue only the two locating pegs on each strap.

panels.title: Keep the seams open
panels.caption: The housing joints, center seam and two thin rear seams stay free of glue.

steps.title: Wire the head harness
actions: Dry-route the loose mouth board and harness to check reach, leaving slack for fitting and removing the mouth. Take them out of the head for soldering and heat-shrink; keep all eye plugs disconnected until the joints are insulated and cool.

Use the second E10 connector pair. Label matching +5 V, GND and DATA contacts, then check continuity through the seated pair. Remove the male header ends from both 5755 leads, keeping their JST-SH plugs.
With the mouth stick loose on the bench, solder and label separate 22 AWG +5 V, GND and DIN leads. Insulate the joints and leave DOUT unused.

Split HEAD +5 V and GND to the first eye’s IN through one Adafruit 5755 lead, and directly to the mouth’s power leads with a separate 22 AWG pair. Solder on the bench and insulate each branch separately.
Join HEAD DATA to the first 5755 lead’s DATA wire on the bench and insulate the splice. Keep its JST-SH plug disconnected for now.
On the bench, join the second 5755 lead’s DATA wire to the mouth DIN lead. Insulate the splice and its unused red and black wires separately.
Check continuity and insulation before connecting the eye plugs. Seat the first 5755 plug in the first eye’s IN; either eye can be first. Press the plug housing rather than its wires.
Use the 100 mm Adafruit 6404 cable from the first eye’s OUT to the second eye’s IN. Seat the second 5755 plug in the second eye’s OUT.
Tie the eye wires at P06 with slack, keeping joints away from bends. Support the wired mouth beside the head until {step:mouth}; do not let it hang from its wires.
steps.check: Mouth power bypasses the eye cable, all joints are insulated, the eye plugs are seated and the wired mouth remains loose for fitting next.

panels.title: Label the HEAD connector
panels.caption: Use the second E10 pair for HEAD. Match contacts by function, not connector sex.

panels.title: Solder the stick on the bench
panels.caption: Adafruit 1426: +5 V, GND and DIN are used; DOUT stays unused.

panels.title: Branch head power
panels.caption: HEAD powers the first eye and mouth separately.

panels.title: Finish the data joints on the bench
panels.caption: First eye 6 → second eye 7 → mouth 8–15. Finish and insulate the harness before connecting its eye plugs.

panels.title: Seat the eye plugs
panels.caption: IN and OUT are marked on the socket side, opposite the LED. Plug in only after the soldering and heat-shrink are complete.

steps.title: Assemble the mouth
actions: With the leads prepared in {step:head-harness}, fit the mouth stick to P30 with two M2×8 screws and M2 nuts, no washers. Support the wired board while working and keep the LED faces unobstructed.
Seat both nuts in the head before bringing in the mouth assembly.
Cut a continuous 4 mm foam strip, 7.4 mm high and slightly long. Curve it into the mouth pocket and trim its ends until it lies flat without bunching or stretching.
Place P31 behind the foam and P30 behind P31. Fit the two outer M2×8 clamp screws from the rear, opposite to the board screws, into the head nuts; no washers.
Check the end LEDs align with their channels and wires, solder and screws clear P31. Leave the gaps empty and tie the wires at P30 without pulling the solder joints.
steps.check: All eight LEDs align behind the smile, the foam lies flat and the cassette can be removed through the open rim.
steps.note: Print P30 and P31 in black PLA. Black plastic is not electrical insulation.

panels.title: Screw the board to P30
panels.caption: Two M2×8 screws enter from the LED/front side into the cassette nuts.

panels.title: Load the head nuts
panels.caption: Two M2 nuts fit the hidden mouth bosses.

panels.title: Fit the foam and separator
panels.caption: P31’s curved face meets the foam; the eight channel openings face the LEDs.

panels.title: Check all eight channels
panels.caption: Leave about 0.7 mm to the LED faces and 2.3 mm to the board.

steps.title: Fit the antenna
actions: Start the large coil thread straight into the head socket and gently hand-tighten until seated.
Support the coil tip and screw the ball on straight by hand. Stop if either thread binds; do not glue them or use the ball as a handle.
steps.check: The antenna base sits flush and the ball unscrews without twisting the coil.
steps.note: You can leave the antenna off until {step:secure-wiring} to protect it while assembling.

panels.title: Hand-tighten both threads
panels.caption: The large A04 thread fits the head; the small tip holds A05.

steps.title: Prepare the head light cable and fasteners
actions: With head and shelf supported separately, test-fit three M2 nuts and three M2×8 button-head screws. Use no washers or plugs; set them aside for {step:head-shoulder-covers}.

Test-route the three-wire HEAD lighting cable through the shelf’s open side notch, clear of the horn screws. Lay it into the notch from the side; do not force the plug through a closed hole. This is separate from the head-servo cable.

Leave a relaxed loop between the rotating head and stationary body. Support both parts and check that the cable lets you lift the head enough to release the HEAD latch. Keep it clear of the horn and screw tips; leave the head and shelf off the servo until the fit-pose step.
steps.check: The fasteners fit freely and the cable can turn and unplug without pulling on an LED board.
steps.note: Head screw seats suit Ø3.5 × 1.3 mm button heads and M2 nuts 4 mm across flats × 1.6 mm thick; check your fasteners.

panels.title: Test the head fasteners
panels.caption: Three M2 nuts load from above P08.

panels.title: Lay the cable into the open entry
panels.caption: The P08 entry opens at the side; lay the cable in from the side.

panels.title: Leave turning and lifting slack
panels.caption: Keep the plug latch reachable below the head.

steps.title: Prepare the body light strand
actions: With the strand unplugged, count six pebbles from INPUT and cut midway between the sixth and seventh. Mark the saved remainder’s newly cut upstream end INPUT before storing it. Label the six lights 0–5.

Keep the BODY connector, R2 and HEAD power tails prepared in {step:body-light-input} attached. If input wiring has not been prepared, make it as shown there before mounting the lights; keep the confirmed INPUT direction.

Dry-route BODY down through the frame’s central opening to H3 in the enclosure, and the separate HEAD power tails up to the head’s side notch. Leave the plugs reachable and enough slack to lift the head and unplug it. Mark any extensions or trimming, then finish them on the bench; keep the existing input branches intact.
On the bench, solder the body half of HEAD to the prepared +5 V and GND tails and light 5’s outgoing DATA. Insulate each joint and the strand’s two unused outgoing power wires individually.
Check connector mapping and that +5 V is not shorted to GND before mounting the strand.

panels.title: Cut from the tested input end
panels.caption: Use only the end positively marked INPUT in {step:body-light-test}.

panels.title: Keep the prepared input wiring
panels.caption: BODY and R2 stay attached after the input test; disconnect H3 while working.

panels.title: Route the separate HEAD power tails
panels.caption: The branches are already soldered. Trim only the free ends for the HEAD connector.

panels.title: Continue only data after light 5
panels.caption: Light 5 DATA OUT joins HEAD DATA; its outgoing power wires remain unused.

steps.title: Fit the six body lights
actions: Fit both P11 brackets and P13 with one M3×10 countersunk screw and M3 nut each.
Hold P12 at the middle rear with low-tack tape, its pads pointing forward and 10° outward. The backpack carrier fastens it in {step:backpack-carrier}.
Place one pebble on each pad with its LED facing out. Pass two ties through the pad slots and gently secure the wire on each side of the resin.
Keep the roughly 100 mm inter-pixel wires in loose loops. Do not cinch, stretch or sharply fold them.
steps.check: All joins are insulated, four lights face forward, the two rear lights angle forward and no tie crosses an LED or resin body.

panels.title: Fit the light brackets
panels.caption: P11 at lower and upper front; P13 at middle front; P12 temporarily taped at middle rear.

panels.title: Tie around the wires, not the LEDs
panels.caption: Two 2.5 mm ties per pebble, outside the resin body.

steps.title: Wrap the body diffuser
actions: Before wrapping the frame, seat M3 nuts in the rear upright’s middle and upper seam-cover pockets.
Cut slightly long, dry-wrap between the collars and trim. Make one slit at each shoulder without removing foam, leaving the horn seats clear.
Fit P09 at the lower and upper rear positions; P12 backs the middle. Temporarily tape the upper P09 in place.
Fit the three P10 covers, fastening only the lower one with one M3×16 screw and nut. Route the servo cables down the frame and through the central hole, clear of pinches and rough edges.
steps.check: The foam sits without stretching and opens at the rear seam; the two upper seam nuts are ready for the carrier.

panels.title: Load rear seam nuts first
panels.caption: Middle and upper M3 nuts will receive the carrier screws later.

panels.title: Wrap and trim the foam
panels.caption: Use the body template: 224.8 × 114.3 mm, 4 mm foam, 2 mm rear seam.

steps.title: Prepare the upper arms
actions: Seat a drilled horn in AR01’s inner round recess. Slide two M2 nuts through the side channels and fasten the drilled hole pair.
Fit the other horn in AR04 with two M2×6 screws and nuts. Keep both arms off the shafts and save their center screws.
steps.check: Both horns sit flat and their center holes are accessible.
steps.note: The arms go onto their shafts only after all three servos reach the fit pose in {step:fit-position}.

panels.title: Robot-left arm AR01
panels.caption: Two M2×6 screws into side-loaded M2 nuts.

panels.title: Robot-right arm AR04
panels.caption: Repeat with the matching arm; keep both center holes open.

steps.title: Build the elbows
actions: Load an M3 nut into each upper arm’s inner elbow pocket. Put the forearm tongue between the fork cheeks and insert the M3×14 screw from outside.
Tighten until the elbow holds a pose but still bends smoothly by hand through 0–70°. Do not squeeze the fork cheeks to force the fit; leave the screw exposed.
steps.check: Both elbows hold their pose and adjust without binding or cracking.

panels.title: Fit the adjustable elbow screws
panels.caption: AR01 + AR02 left; AR04 + AR05 right. One M3×14 screw and M3 nut per elbow.

steps.title: Fit the hands and test-fit the shoulder covers
actions: Dry-fit all four magnets and check that each forearm–hand pair attracts. Mark the forearm mating faces A and the hand mating faces B, as shown; these are temporary marks for opposite poles. Repeat for both arms.
Use the two-part epoxy to glue the magnets into their recesses. Keep the parts apart until it has fully cured.
Push each hand in by its palm and turn it to a pose. Check it seats fully and stays on. To remove it, pull the palm straight out.
Optional AR07 replaces the robot-left AR03 hand and needs one additional magnet with the same hand polarity.
Test-fit AR08, then remove it so the servo center screw remains accessible.
Test-fit AR09 and remove it too. Keep both arms on the bench.
steps.check: Hands hold their pose and both shoulder covers fit and remove freely.

panels.title: Check the magnet pairs
panels.caption: One 3/16 × 1/16-inch disc magnet in each forearm and hand.

panels.title: Glue and let the magnets cure
panels.caption: Keep glue off the wrist peg, socket and end stops.

panels.title: Seat each hand by its palm
panels.caption: The magnet retains the hand; friction holds its angle.

panels.title: Try the left cover
panels.caption: AR08 is robot-left.

panels.title: Try the right cover
panels.caption: AR09 is robot-right.

steps.title: Fit the backpack carrier
actions: Load all four side-entry nuts before fitting the shell; they receive its four screws in the next step.
Place P34 against the middle and upper seam covers. Align the stacked holes and start both screws into the nuts loaded in {step:body-diffuser}.
Tighten evenly, then remove the temporary tape. Keep the shell off until both carrier screws are secure.
steps.check: Both screws pass through the full stack, the carrier follows the body curve and its four shell nuts remain seated.

panels.title: Load four shell nuts
panels.caption: Four M3 nuts enter the carrier from its sides.

panels.title: Fasten carrier to frame
panels.caption: Two M3×18 screws pass through P34, seam covers and P12 or upper P09 into the rear upright.

steps.title: Build and attach the backpack
actions: Seat the tanks in P35 and fasten them before fitting the nozzle plugs.
Fit each elbow’s lower pin into its tank dome and side pin into the rolled top edge. Dry-fit P37 nozzle plugs and P40 top band without force.
When all parts seat and the tank screws remain accessible, glue the plugs, elbows and top band with the two-part epoxy. Allow full cure.
Fit the shell and all four screws. Keep the two lower belt docks clear.
steps.check: Tanks and details are secure, and the shell removes backward after its four screws are removed.

panels.title: Fasten both tanks first
panels.caption: One M3×8 screw and M3 nut per P36 tank.

panels.title: Dry-fit the details
panels.caption: P38 is the left elbow; P39 is the right. Lower pins point down, side pins inward.

panels.title: Fasten the shell to P34
panels.caption: Four M3×12 screws into the preloaded carrier nuts.

steps.title: Assemble the belt
actions: Arrange the seven links in the pictured order with the buckle frame facing outward. Use B09 pins, identified by three small head notches.
Nest each knuckle in the next fork and insert a B09 pin from above. Six pins join the seven links.
Nest each rear link between the tabs on P35 and insert the remaining two B09 pins from above. Keep the links free to pivot.
Check every joint pivots and each head sits just below the top edge. To open later, support each rear link and push its pin upward from below with a spare pin.
steps.check: The belt pivots without cracking and both rear joints open without bending the side bands.

panels.title: Arrange the seven links
panels.caption: Starting at left rear: B01 → B02 → B02 → B03 → B02 → B02 → B04.

panels.title: Insert the pins from above
panels.caption: B02–B02 joint shown; use the same pin direction for the six link joints.

panels.title: Pin both ends to the backpack
panels.caption: P35 and B01 shown; repeat with B04 on the other side.

steps.title: Connect the three servo cables
actions: Support the robot in its stand. Bring the BASE→BODY lighting lead and three separately labeled servo cables through the smooth central opening into the enclosure. Keep each cable identifiable; connect LEFT to the shown ports.
Connect RIGHT, then gently pull-check both WAGO wires and its signal wire.
Connect the head servo. Keep its cable distinct from the separate HEAD lighting plug.

panels.title: Land the left servo
panels.caption: LEFT: W2/2 +5 V, W4/2 GND, S1 C5 signal.

panels.title: Land the right servo
panels.caption: RIGHT: W2/3 +5 V, W4/3 GND, S2 D5 signal.

panels.title: Land the head servo
panels.caption: HEAD servo: W2/4 +5 V, W4/4 GND, S2 C5 signal.

steps.title: Connect the light connectors and secure the cables
actions: Connect BASE→BODY. H3 DATA already lands on S1 D5; F2 and C2 stay in the base. Support the head separately on the bench and connect HEAD without letting a cable carry its weight.
Check labels and connector mapping, closed levers and no sustained +5 V-to-ground short. A meter cannot check data through an LED; the next light test checks the full chain.

Secure stationary bundles with P13 and adhesive tie mounts, leaving the HEAD lighting loop free to turn and both lighting latches reachable. Leave enough service slack to reach servo terminals without pulling a splice. Keep splices off bends, clear of moving horns, and away from WAGO levers, SD card, microphone and frame screws.
steps.check: All three servos match their labels, lighting plugs are seated and no cable or joint takes tension.

panels.title: Seat the lighting plugs
panels.caption: BASE→BODY supplies the body; HEAD continues power and data to the head lighting.

panels.title: Keep moving cables free
panels.caption: Keep slack at plugs and the head, clear of screws and the open shelf entry.

steps.title: Inspect before power-up
actions: Check connector polarity, capacitor polarity and that neither speaker output joins ground.
Remove F1 and check no direct W1-to-W2 bypass exists. Refit T3.15 A and confirm that the path now passes through it; confirm F2 is T1 A.
Inspect WAGO levers, terminals, screw tips, nuts, washers and every cable crossing. Remove all wire offcuts and debris.
Keep head and arms off the shafts and supported separately. Check the frame is stable and take a wiring photo for future repairs.
steps.check: No sustained shorts, reversed connections, loose joints or trapped wires; servos are mounted with bare shafts.

panels.title: Recheck power after the new wiring
panels.caption: Remove F1 to distinguish a fuse path from an accidental direct link.

panels.title: Check connectors and fasteners
panels.caption: No loose strands, partially seated plugs or pinched wires.

steps.title: Power up and test all 16 lights

safety.text: Keep the supply plug reachable. Never open a WAGO lever with power connected.

actions: Support the robot on its stand with the cover off, head on the bench and HEAD connected. Keep head and arms off the servo shafts; fit F1 T3.15 A and F2 T1 A.
Connect the specified supply to the robot, then the wall. Bare servo shafts may turn to their rest positions.

After boot, check make pi-status shows “active (running)”. Run make pi-ssh, then vcgencmd get_throttled; expect throttled=0x0. Type exit. If it reports a warning, use Troubleshooting before continuing.
Run make pi-test-neopixels. Check that all 16 lights appear in order and show red, green and blue. If a light is missing or out of order, check its input and output connections.
Run make pi-ssh, then sudo poweroff. Wait for the green light to stop flashing and unplug the supply.
steps.check: All 16 lights show the correct order and colors, and the Pi starts without a power warning.

panels.title: Power the robot
panels.caption: Keep the head and arms off the servo shafts.

panels.title: Check startup and all 16 lights
panels.caption: Body 0–5 → first eye 6 → second eye 7 → mouth 8–15.

steps.title: Set the fit position
actions: Stand the robot upright, cover off, with the prepared head shelf, head and arms nearby. Keep the horns off all three shafts.
Power up and wait for the Pi. Run make pi-servo-fit on your computer; it stops the application, positions all three servos and holds them.
When movement stops, type STOP and press Enter. Run make pi-ssh, then sudo poweroff; wait for the green light to stop and unplug. Do not turn the shafts by hand.

panels.title: Command the fit pose
panels.caption: Head centered; both shoulder shafts positioned for arms hanging down.

steps.title: Attach the head shelf and arms
actions: With the shelf front toward the robot front, seat its horn on the nearest spline tooth and fit the center screw. Never pull a misaligned horn onto the spline with the screw.
Seat the left arm’s horn on the nearest spline tooth with the arm hanging down. Fit its supplied center screw.
Seat and fasten the right arm the same way, using its supplied center screw.
steps.note: A 21-tooth spline gives about 17° between teeth. Pick the closest tooth; do not force a horn or bend an arm to correct the small remaining offset.

panels.title: Attach the head shelf
panels.caption: Use the servo’s supplied center screw, not an M2 screw.

panels.title: Attach the robot-left arm
panels.caption: AR01 hangs straight down at the fit pose.

panels.title: Attach the robot-right arm
panels.caption: AR04 hangs straight down at the fit pose.

steps.title: Fasten the head and shoulder covers
actions: Place the three M2 nuts in P08 from above. Keep the HEAD plug seated and accessible, then lower the head without trapping its cable.
Start all three head screws by hand and tighten just enough to secure the shell.
Fit AR08 after checking the left arm center screw is secure.
Fit AR09 and check both arms hang down and the head faces forward.
steps.check: All three center screws are fitted, the head is secure and the cable has slack.

panels.title: Route HEAD and load the nuts
panels.caption: Lay the cable into P08’s open side entry and leave turning/lifting slack.

panels.title: Fasten the head
panels.caption: Three M2×8 button-head screws, no washers or plugs.

panels.title: Close the left shoulder
panels.caption: AR08 covers the robot-left center screw.

panels.title: Close the right shoulder
panels.caption: AR09 covers the robot-right center screw.

steps.title: Check the first movement
actions: Stand the robot upright with the cover off and room around it. Clear fingers, tools and cables, then power it on.
The application moves the servos to the same rest pose you just fitted, so expect little movement.

Press the button and talk to the robot, then ask it to dance. Watch the HEAD lighting loop as the head turns: it must stay loose without catching a horn, screw or edge. Check the other cables for rubbing, stretching or contact with moving parts.
If anything binds or strains, unplug immediately. Free the cable or refit the part using {step:fit-position}, then repeat. F1 does not protect a jammed servo.
steps.check: Conversation and dance movements clear the body, head and wiring.
steps.note: Software limits arms from hanging down to roughly level forward, and the head to about 45° either side. Correct mechanical horn positioning is still required.

panels.title: Start from the fitted rest pose
panels.caption: The arms start hanging down; the head starts facing forward.

panels.title: Watch a conversation and a dance
panels.caption: Check clearance around both arms, hands, head and cables.

steps.title: Secure the wiring before closing
actions: After the movement check, shut down with make pi-ssh and sudo poweroff. Wait for the green light to stop, unplug the supply and support the robot in its padded stand.
Close every WAGO lever. Check that plugs are fully seated, insulation covers the joints and cable ties support the wires without pulling on connections.
Tuck loose wires and tie locks away from the screw holes and foot posts. Keep them at least 4 mm from the inside face of the bottom cover.
steps.check: Connections are seated and insulated, and the cover can close without pressing on the wiring.

panels.title: Secure the wires and clear the cover

steps.title: Fit the bottom cover
actions: Keep the robot unplugged and supported in its padded stand.
Check that no wire crosses the cover edge or a screw hole.
Seat FB02 around the foot posts. If it resists, remove it and correct the obstruction; do not pull it down with screws.
Fasten the cover, then stand the robot upright on all four feet with its vents clear.
steps.check: The cover sits flat without pressing on wiring and the robot rests level on its feet.
steps.note: The four cover nuts were fitted in {step:board-cover-nuts}.

panels.title: Seat the cover by hand
panels.caption: All electronics and feet stay on FB01; nothing attaches to FB02.

panels.title: Fit all four screws
panels.caption: Four M3×12 screws into the glued M3 nuts.

steps.title: Try your finished robot
actions: Stand the robot upright with its vents clear. Connect the supply to the robot, then the wall, and wait for the Pi to boot. Press the front button and have a short conversation. Check that it hears you and that speech sounds clear.
Ask it to wave and play its dance. Check that the head and arms move freely, cables stay clear of the joints, and the body and eye lights respond.
If something does not work, use Troubleshooting below. Shut down the Pi and unplug the supply before opening the base or adjusting wiring.
steps.check: Conversation, sound, movement and lighting work with the cover fitted.

steps.title: Open the head
actions: Shut down and unplug. Support the head, remove its three screws, and lift only far enough to unplug HEAD. Take the head to the bench without pulling an LED wire.
Keep nuts with their screws. On refitting, lay the cable in the side entry, leave slack and tighten the same screws without washers or plugs.

panels.title: Lift the head off its shelf
panels.caption: Section view of one joint. Remove the three M2×8 head screws; leave the three M3×8 adapter screws fitted.

panels.title: Keep the shelf nuts together
panels.caption: The three M2 nuts load from above when the head is off.

steps.title: Remove the mouth or an eye housing
actions: Open the head as in {step:head-open}. Support P30, remove its two outer M2×8 clamp screws and move the cassette back, then down through the open rim. Release ties for slack; never pull on soldered leads.
Remove P31 and the foam afterward. Remove the two board screws only on the bench.
Unplug the eye leads, support the housing and remove its two outer M2×10 screws and washers. The central M2×6 board screws can stay.
Pull the cassette backward and slide the housing straight out, catching its nuts. Refit eyes before mouth, with nuts loaded from the housing’s upper edge and no glue.

panels.title: Remove the mouth cassette
panels.caption: P30 and its board move backward about 8 mm, then down. P31 and foam remain until afterward.

panels.title: Remove an eye housing
panels.caption: Remove the mouth first for straight access to the outer eye screws.

steps.title: Service a hand, elbow or shoulder
actions: Shut down and unplug. Support the forearm and pull a hand straight out by its palm, never by a finger.
Adjust elbow stiffness at its exposed M3×14 screw; the joint should hold a pose and still bend smoothly by hand.
Remove the shoulder cover to access the servo center screw. If a horn comes off, use {step:fit-position} to refit it.
steps.check: Removed parts are supported and fasteners stay together for refitting.

panels.title: Reach the shoulder center screw
panels.caption: The right shoulder opens in the same way.

steps.title: Open the base and remove boards
actions: Shut down, unplug and support base, head and arms in the padded stand. Remove the four cover screws and lift FB02 off.
For the SD card, release a nearby tie if needed and grip the card through its access gap; leave the Pi mounted.
For the Pi, label and unplug power, USB and GPIO leads, then remove its screws. Repair any loose nut bond with the board out and let it cure.
Label and release its wires, then remove its two screws. Cut the Neo jumper on either replacement board (S1 or S2) before fitting it.
Label and release its wires. Support the connector and follow the tape maker’s removal method; do not lever against a printed pad. Refit with fresh tape and check the bond before wiring.
Recheck any changed wiring, seat FB02 by hand and refit its four screws. Stand the robot upright for a function check.
steps.check: The repair is checked, all cables are supported and the cover closes without pressing on them.

panels.title: Remove the cover
panels.caption: Four M3×12 screws release FB02; nothing is connected to it.

panels.title: Reach the SD card or remove the Pi
panels.caption: Four M2×12 screws secure the Pi.

panels.title: Remove a shifter
panels.caption: Two M2×10 screws per shifter.

panels.title: Remove a WAGO
panels.caption: Release wires before separating the tape bond.

panels.title: Close after repair
panels.caption: Restore insulation, labels and strain relief before closing.

steps.title: Replace a fuse, capacitor or power jack
actions: Shut down, unplug and confirm capacitor voltage has discharged before touching power wiring. Label connections before releasing them.
Cut retaining ties as needed, shielding wires from the cutter. Open the holder in your hand and fit the same fuse value. Release a WAGO wire if needed for slack; never pull a holder by its wires.
Release its two WAGO wires and retaining ties. Prepare the replacement on the bench, insulate each polarity, then refit with its vent uncovered and body supported.
Unplug BASE→BODY and release the lighting lead for bench work. Preserve C2 polarity and separate insulation, then support the repaired body and wires with fresh ties.
Release the J1 leads at W1/1 and W3/1 and their restraint, then remove the plate screws. Do not twist the solder lugs.
Recheck polarity, continuity, fuse values and insulation before powering the repaired base.
steps.check: Specified fuses, correct polarity, insulation and wire restraint are restored.

panels.title: Replace F1 or F2
panels.caption: F1 is T3.15 A; F2 is T1 A.

panels.title: Replace C1
panels.caption: C1 + → W2/5; striped negative → W3/4.

panels.title: Replace C2 or its lighting branch
panels.caption: C2 is soldered into H3 on the base side of BASE→BODY.

panels.title: Remove the inlet plate
panels.caption: Two M3×12 screws release FB21 and its jack together.

steps.title: Service audio, speakers or button
actions: With power unplugged, disconnect USB and speaker plugs by their bodies. Remove the two lid screws and lid. Support the case and cradle while releasing the tape according to the tape maker’s removal instructions; then lift out the module.

Remove the empty cradle only after the module. If any of its three base nuts comes loose, refit and glue it as shown in {step:cradle-jack-nuts}; let the glue cure before reinstalling the cradle. Replace the tape before refitting the case as shown in {step:audio-module}.
Support the grille, remove the outer screws and move it only as far as its cable slack allows. Unplug the speaker and replace it on the bench, preserving tab washers and nuts.
Keep switch and LED wires labeled separately. On refitting, seat the retaining nut in its recess and let the insert sit flush before tightening.
Keep microphone and speaker openings clear, restore the lid foam, then test sound with the robot upright.
steps.check: The serviced parts are secure, plugs seat fully and all sound openings remain clear.

panels.title: Remove the audio module
panels.caption: Two M2×8 lid screws release FB32.

panels.title: Remove the cradle
panels.caption: Three M3×6 screws; the middle one is beneath the module.

panels.title: Remove a speaker
panels.caption: Four outer M3×12 screws release the grille; four inner screws hold its speaker.

panels.title: Remove the button
panels.caption: Disconnect four quick-connect bodies, then remove two M3×8 plate screws.

steps.title: Replace a servo
actions: Shut down, unplug and open the base in the service stand. Identify the cable by labels and disconnect only the servo being replaced.
For a right-shoulder replacement, release these three labeled connections.
For a head-servo replacement, release these three connections; the separate HEAD lighting plug is not a servo lead.
Release cable ties as needed. Support the arm or head, remove the center screw and lift its horn off without forcing the shaft.
Remove bracket-to-frame screws if access requires it, then the two M2 ear screws and nuts. Slide the servo sideways out of the open bracket.
Prepare its cable as in {step:servo-cables}, mount and reconnect the new servo, and leave its horn off.
Follow {step:fit-position}: command the fit pose, STOP, shut down and unplug, then refit the horn and part. Repeat {step:first-movement}.
steps.check: The replacement is secure, the horn was fitted at the commanded pose and all movement is clear.

panels.title: Disconnect LEFT if replacing it
panels.caption: LEFT: W2/2, W4/2 and S1 C5.

panels.title: RIGHT connection reference
panels.caption: RIGHT: W2/3, W4/3 and S2 D5.

panels.title: HEAD connection reference
panels.caption: HEAD servo: W2/4, W4/4 and S2 C5.

panels.title: Remove the horn and servo
panels.caption: Shoulder bracket shown. Both shoulder and head servos use two M2×6 ear screws; support the attached part before removing its horn center screw.

panels.title: Refit in the commanded pose
panels.caption: A replacement needs the same positioning sequence as the original build.

steps.title: Replace an eye board or mouth stick
actions: Shut down and unplug power. Support the head, remove its three M2×8 screws and lift only far enough to unplug HEAD before taking it to the bench.

Remove the mouth as in {step:mouth-eye-removal} for tool access. Unplug the eye leads and remove the two M2×6 board screws. Keep the cassette fitted if its board nuts stay seated; if a nut moves, withdraw the cassette and reseat it on the bench.

Fit the replacement board with LED toward foam and sockets inward, preserving IN/OUT. For housing or cassette replacement, remove the two outer screws as in {step:mouth-eye-removal}. Refit the eyes before the mouth.
Remove P30 as in {step:mouth-eye-removal}, then replace and solder the Adafruit 1426 on the bench. Connect +5 V, GND and DIN only; DOUT remains unused.

panels.title: Disconnect the lighting plugs
panels.caption: HEAD isolates head lighting; BASE→BODY isolates the body from the base.

panels.title: Replace an eye board
panels.caption: Adafruit 5975 has separate IN and OUT sockets.

panels.title: Replace the mouth stick
panels.caption: Retain the dedicated 22 AWG head power pair; mouth power does not pass through eye leads.

steps.title: Replace the body lights
actions: Shut down and unplug power. Unplug BASE→BODY and HEAD, open the foam seam and release ties. Remove the strand with its head power feed.

For six replacement lights from your marked saved remainder, retain the marked input direction. Transfer the existing BODY connector, R2 and HEAD power feed on the bench, using the input joints in {step:body-light-input}; then follow {step:body-light-strand} for cutting, output joins and mounting.

For an entirely new strand, transfer the BODY/R2 harness and its HEAD power tails to the likely input as in {step:body-light-input}. Keep the HEAD connector unplugged; do not dismantle the head harness or buy another connector pair.

Remove F1 and label and disconnect all three servo cables using {step:servo-replacement}. Follow the input test in {step:body-light-test}, leaving the prepared input harness attached after a passing test. Then build the six-light section as in {step:body-light-strand}.
Restore the labeled servo connections and F1, and repeat the unpowered checks and all-16-light test before closing.
steps.check: Replaced lights follow the correct power and data paths, and no wire carries the weight of a removed part.

panels.title: Replace the body strand
panels.caption: Six pebbles form one strand; two ties per pebble retain wires outside the resin.

panels.title: Test a new replacement strand
panels.caption: Test through the permanent BODY/R2 input; keep HEAD unplugged.

panels.title: Restore and test the complete chain
